IS: 9631 -1983 



Indian Standard 



( Reaffirmed 1998) 




SPECIFICATION FOR 

GAUGING MEMBERS FOR GO AND NO GO SCREW 

PLUG GAUGES AND SCREW CHECK PLUG GAUGES 

FOR ISO METRIC SCREW THREADS 

(SIZE RANGE FROM M1 UP TO AND INCLUDING M40) 

( First Revision ) 



1 . Scope — Covers requirements for gauging members for GO and NO GO screw plug gauges and GO 
and NO GO screw check plug gauges for GO and NO GO new solid screw ring gauges in the size 
range from M1 up to and including M40 for ISO metric screw threads according to IS : 4218 ( Parts 1 
to 6 ) ' ISO metric screw threads '. 

2. Material — Shall be as prescribed in IS : 7018 (Part1)-1983 ' Technical supply conditions for 
gauges: Part 1 General ( first revision ) '. 

3. Dimensions — The dimensions and tolerances shall be as specified in Table 1 read with Fig. 1 to 4. 

3.1 The dimensions and tolerances shown in the table apply to the gauging members that have been 
hardened and finished on the taper shanks but left oversize on the gauging diameter for subsequent 
completion to the required sizes. The amount of excess material left to allow for finishing to size is at 
the discretion of the gauge manufacturers. 

3.2 Centres — Gauging members up to and including M3 diameter may be ground with a ground 60° 
external centre at gauging end as shown in Fig. 1 and a female centre at shank end.

3.2.1 Gauging members of all other sizes shall have a female centre in accordance with 
IS : 2473-1975 ' Dimensions for centre holes (first revision ) '. On sizes above M14 nominal diameter, 
a small protection recess is desirable. 

4. Gauging Dimensions and Thread Profile — Shall conform to IS:2334-1975 'Gauging practice 
for ISO metric screw threads ( first revision ) '. 

5. Taper Shanks — Shall have a good finish and made to fit the taper ring gauge applicable to its 
size according to IS : 9529-1980 ' Taper plug gauges and taper ring gauges to check taper bore of 
gauge handles and taper shanks of gauging members '. 

6. Dirt Grooves — Dirt grooves shall be provided where necessary for GO members from M12 up to 
M40. The dirt grooves with 'U' shape shall have width 2 mm and the depth of the dirt grooves shall 
be such that it clears the minor diameter of the plug gauges. 

7. Designation 

7.1 Gauging members shall be designated by the name of the gauging member GO or NO GO, nominal 
diameter, pitch and the tolerance class. If the pitch is not indicated in the designation, coarse pitch 
is implied. 

Examples : 

a) A GO or NO GO gauging member of screw plug gauge of nominal diameter M16, pitch 1'5 mm 
and tolerance class 6H shall be designated as : 

GO Gauging Member M16 x 1*5 — 6H IS : 9631 

NO GO Gauging Member M16 x 1*5 — 6H IS : 9631

Note 2 — The relief diameter for M1 to M3 and M3 to M6 ranges shall be smaller than the core diameter of thread.

8. General Requirements 

8.1 Other requirements for gauging members, not covered in this standard, shall be as given in 
IS : 7018 (Part 1 )-1983. 

8.2 The gauge handles shall be according to IS : 5388-1983 ' Specification for hexagon handles for 
plain and threaded plug gauges ( second revision ) '. 

8.3 NO GO gauging members shall carry red paint on the groove between the gauging portion and the 
shank as indicated in Fig. 1. . 

9. Marking — Shall be in conformity with IS : 7018 (Part 1 )-1983. 

9.1 iSi Certification Marking — Details .available with the Indian Standards Institution. 



EXPLANATORY NOTE 

This standard was first published in 1980. It has now been revised to bring it in line with the 
latest manufacturing practices prevalent in India. Alterations have been made in Fig. 1 to 4 and the 
clauses on designation. 

The taper lock design is particularly suitable for the smaller sizes of plug gauges. This type of 
gauge \i economical to produce and maintain. 

It is a feature of the taper lock system that the gauging members are firmly locked in the handle 
by engagement of the taper shanks in the taper holes and when properly made and assembled, they 
have the rigidity of solid gauges. Dimensions and tolerances for the mating parts of gauging members 
and handles have been chosen so as to ensure full interchangeability of these parts wherever 
manufactured. 

A drift slot or hole is provided near one end of the handle, preferably near the GO member, to 
enable the gauging member to be removed when replacement is necessary. In the case of double 
ended gauges, the second member is removed by running a rod through the hollow handle. 

For the convenience of manufacture, the NO GO member made from GO blank is shown in Fig. 4. 
This reduces the inventory of gauge blanks. Blanks for NO GO gauges shall be selected from the 
short or medium series so that there are not less than four completed threads. The blank may be 
relieved as shown in the figure if necessary. 

Chamfer details on measuring faces and radius at the end of taper shanks are covered. 

The requirements of gauging members above M40 and up to-and including M120 sizes have been 
covered in a separate specification IS : 9608-1980 ' Specification for gauges members for GO and NO 
GO screw plug gauges and screw check plug gauges for ISO metric screw threads (size range above 
M40 up to and including M120) '. 

In the preparation of this standard, considerable assistance has been derived from ISO 3670-1979 
' Blanks for plug gauges and handles ( taper lock and trilock ) and ring gauges — design and general 
dimensions \ issued by the International Organization for Standardization. 



Printed at Printrade, New Delhi, India
